units: <cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:1">Ab. V, 1</cite> <he>והלא במ׳ אחד וכ׳</he> could not the universe have been created by one divine command?—
<cite ref="Megillah 21b:9">Meg. 21ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 32a:19">R. Hash. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>בראשית נמי מ׳ הוא</he> the first verse of Genesis is also to be considered a command.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 4:6">Gen. R. s. 4</cite> <he>המים … תלוים במ׳</he> the upper waters are suspended (in the air) by a divine ordainment; <cite ref="Taanit 10a">Taan. 10ᵃ</cite>.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 63a:21">Sabb. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>העושה מצוה כמַאֲמָרָהּ</he> who executes a divine command as it has been ordained; a. e.—Pl. <he>מַאֲמָרוֹת</he>. Ab. l. c. <he>בעשרה מ׳ וכ׳</he> the world was created by ten divine orders (counting nine <he>ויאמר</he> in <cite ref="Genesis 1:1">Gen. ch. I</cite>, and the first verse, v. supra).

senses.gloss: word, esp. maămar, the Yabam’s betrothal (v. יָבָם) by word of mouth, contrad. to the consummation of marriage (בִּיאָה).
units: Yeb. II, 1 עשה בה מ׳ if he betrothed her to himself; Y. ib. 3ᶜ איזו היא מ׳ וכ׳ what is a maămar with regard to a Y’bamah? Saying, ‘Be betrothed unto me’, while handing to her money or money’s worth. Ib. מ׳ גומר betrothal consummates the yabam’s marriage (carrying with it all the legal consequences of his marriage), v. גָּמַר; a. v. fr.
